summary:
Trends is the category to lean on across every rating today — all four models show identical 8-4 (67%, n=12) marks over the last 14 days with a 4-game winning streak, and it's not a small-sample mirage: trends sits at 56% on 1113 decisions for R1-R3 and 58% on 442 for R4, the best season baseline of any category. Hitting is right there too, running hot at 67% for R1/R2/R3 across the same window, while SP is the clear fade — 33% (4-8) across the board with R1/R2/R3 all carrying a 3-game winning streak that masks the category's rough patch, and bullpen is ice cold at 42% with a 3-game losing streak on all three full-season ratings. R2 is the rating to trust most right now: it's hitting 100% (3-0, +3.0u) over the last 7 days and 67% (4-2, +1.0u) over 14, the best short-term P/L of the group, with a season mark of 56% and +79.0u on 471 strong plays. R4's small sample (0 plays in 7 days, 1 loss in 14) means don't overweight its strong-play signal today — stick with R1-R3 where trends and hitting both light up.

On today's board, prioritize games where trends and hitting agree — both are running 67% hot simultaneously, and trends+sp (57.8%, n=635) and trends+runs (57.1%, n=700) remain the two best category combos all season, so any slate game where R1, R2, or R3 has trends aligned with either sp or runs is the highest-confidence spot even though sp itself is cold individually; the combo signal overrides the raw category streak. Team-wise, if LAD or BOS show up as model-liked teams today, lean in hard — LAD is 80% (28-7, +27.0u) on strong plays and BOS is 76% (22-7, +19.0u), both best-in-class. Avoid letting NYY backdoor into a strong play — model likes them just 49% overall and strong plays are upside-down at 39% (-4.0u), the only team on the leaderboard bleeding units when backed hard. If NYY and a bullpen-driven rating intersect today, that's the single biggest red flag on the board: cold category, cold team.
